name: Help and Documentation
description: Even highly usable products sometimes need help content; good documentation is easy to search, focused on concrete tasks, concise, and available at the moment of need rather than assuming users will read a manual front to back.
design_relevance_note: Shows up in setup guides, searchable help centers, inline hints, empty-state guidance, admin/enterprise onboarding, and recovery flows where users need support without leaving the task.
myth_risk_note: Real evidence exists that task-focused documentation improves learning, consistent with this entry's existing partial backing. This pass's evidence for contextual help effectiveness and localization moves modestly in the same direction rather than adding a large new evidence base.
prevalence_note: Named directly in Nielsen's 10 heuristics and still common in enterprise/software products where setup, exceptions, and advanced workflows require searchable support material.

findings.description: Contextual help (instructions/highlights shown directly on the interface rather than in a separate viewer) is effective for learning GUIs, but end-users and third-party tech support typically cannot author it themselves without programming skill and source-code access. A screenshot-based authoring tool addressing this gap was evaluated for usability with developers, instructors, and tech support, and validated against 60 real university tech-support tasks -- real-world evidence that in-context, task-focused help support has practical value beyond what conventional documentation provides.
findings.source_title: Creating contextual help for GUIs using screenshots
findings.source_venue: Proceedings of the 24th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '11)

findings.description: Two controlled experiments comparing a deliberately brief, error-recovery-focused 'Minimal Manual' against an otherwise comparable commercial self-instruction manual found the minimal version produced more efficient learning progress, specifically in the areas its design predicted. Supports the underlying premise behind the 'paradox of the active user': people learning new software tend to start doing rather than read comprehensive instructions first, so documentation built around that behavior (short, task-focused, strong on error recovery) outperforms documentation that assumes people will read it start to finish.

applications.title: Dyson's video-only setup instructions, with no text alternative
applications.description: Dyson's product setup instructions were provided only as video tutorials, with no accompanying text-based steps -- even though captions were available within the video. NN/g cites this as a reactive-help failure: users who prefer to scan written steps, or who can't or don't want to watch a video, have no alternative, reducing the visibility and interaction efficiency of the help content.
applications.ethical_note: This is a straightforward accessibility and format-completeness gap in help content, not a persuasion or dark-pattern case -- there is no competing interest between Dyson and its users that a text-instructions omission would serve; it reads as an oversight rather than a deliberate choice, included alongside the Microsoft Word example as a matched negative counterpart.

applications.title: Groupize's 'G.G.' gamified onboarding assistant, shortlisted for a real industry award
applications.description: Userpilot's own case study describes how Groupize (a real travel/events-management SaaS platform), working with Justin Peticolas (Groupize's named Manager of Implementation and Onboarding), gamified their user onboarding by building 'G.G.' (Groupize Guide) -- an in-app assistant persona (styled like Siri or Alexa) that guides users through onboarding tours, checklists, and contextual help. The initiative was shortlisted for the Skift Idea Awards 2022, a real named travel-industry design/innovation award. Groupize reported a qualitative shift in support-ticket patterns after launch: routine 'how do I' questions dropped as G.G. handled them, leaving human support to focus on genuinely complex issues.
applications.ethical_note: A gamified assistant persona built to help users self-serve and reduce their own support friction, not to manipulate spending or extract engagement against users' own interest.

applications.title: Microsoft Word's contextual resume tip: a well-timed 'pull revelation'
applications.description: When Microsoft Word recognizes a user is working on a resume, it surfaces a contextual tip offering resume suggestions from LinkedIn -- triggered by the user's own behavior rather than shown to everyone at launch, illustrating a 'pull revelation': proactive help that is timely and relevant because it responds to what the specific user is actually doing.
applications.ethical_note: Contextual help triggered by what the user is actually doing serves the user's own goal (finishing a resume) with no competing business interest steering the suggestion -- a straightforward case of proactive help done well, included as the positive half of a pair with the Dyson example in this same wave.
